question: Should ClawSweeper formally own advisory release-train scope reporting using the proposed contract, metadata authority, and staged shadow rollout?
rationale: Only maintainers can assign release-policy ownership, approve the authoritative metadata and exception model, and decide whether the lane may progress from local audit to public reporting or later enforcement.

options.title: Sponsor staged advisory rollout
options.body: Approve the contract and read-only audit first, then review durable publishing and non-blocking checks as separate stages before one complete shadow train.

options.title: Approve local audit only
options.body: Accept deterministic local Markdown and JSON reports but keep durable publication and pull-request checks out of scope.

options.title: Decline ClawSweeper ownership
options.body: Keep release-train scope decisions and reporting entirely within OpenClaw's existing release process.

recommendation.title: Sponsor staged advisory rollout
recommendation.body: Approve the contract and read-only audit first, then review durable publishing and non-blocking checks as separate stages before one complete shadow train.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice concerns release-governance ownership rather than implementation mechanics, and the available policy discussion points to Peter.
